questiontext.text:
Prove that if \(p\) is a prime number with \(p \gt 3\), then \(p^2 - 1\) is a multiple of 24.

Drag blocks into order to make a proof. Not every block is needed: two of the blocks contain a mistake. Any order in which each step comes after the steps it relies on is accepted.

[[parsons input="ans1"]] {"steps": {# parsons_encode(proof_steps) #}, "headers": ["Your proof:"], "available_header": ["Drag from here:"]} [[/parsons]]
[[input:ans1]] [[validation:ans1]]

generalfeedback.text:
One correct proof:

Let \(p\) be a prime number with \(p \gt 3\).

Then \(p^2 - 1 = (p - 1)(p + 1)\).

Since \(p\) is a prime greater than 2, \(p\) is odd, so \(p - 1\) and \(p + 1\) are consecutive even numbers.

Of two consecutive even numbers, one is a multiple of 4 and the other is a multiple of 2, so \((p - 1)(p + 1)\) is a multiple of \(4 \times 2 = 8\).

Of the three consecutive integers \(p - 1\), \(p\), \(p + 1\), exactly one is a multiple of 3.

Since \(p\) is a prime greater than 3, \(p\) is not a multiple of 3. So \(p - 1\) or \(p + 1\) is a multiple of 3, and \((p - 1)(p + 1)\) is a multiple of 3.

So \(p^2 - 1\) is a multiple of 8 and a multiple of 3. Since 8 and 3 have no common factor other than 1, \(p^2 - 1\) is a multiple of \(8 \times 3 = 24\).

The part that finds the factor 8 and the part that finds the factor 3 are independent, so they can come in either order, or interleaved; the factorisation can come anywhere before the conclusion.

The two blocks with mistakes: two consecutive even numbers are not both multiples of 4 (4 and 6), and a multiple of two numbers need not be a multiple of their product (12 is a multiple of 4 and of 6, but not of 24). The first part of the proof is the result for odd numbers from the chapter on the structure of a proof; the second is the argument of the three-consecutive-integers example in this chapter.

node.description: A valid order of the correct blocks

truefeedback.text: Yes. The factor 8 and the factor 3 come from independent parts of the proof, and 8 and 3 have no common factor other than 1, so together they give 24.

node.description: Diagnostic: a block with a mistake used

truefeedback.text:
[[if test="useddboth"]]

One of your blocks says that two consecutive even numbers are both multiples of 4. That is false: 4 and 6 are consecutive even numbers, and 6 is not a multiple of 4. Exactly one of the two is.

[[/if]][[if test="useddrule"]]

One of your blocks says that a multiple of two numbers is always a multiple of their product. That is false: 12 is a multiple of 4 and of 6, but not of 24. The step from 8 and 3 to 24 works because 8 and 3 have no common factor other than 1.

[[/if]]
